title: 2nd Mystery The Equality Of Few And Many Through The Mystery Of Luminosity And Obedience

questions.question: What is the main idea of the Second Mystery?
questions.answer: Allah’s power can act on countless things as easily as on one thing.

questions.question: What three qualities are mentioned at the start of the passage to explain this mystery?
questions.answer: Brightness, clearness, and obedience.

questions.question: How does the example of the sun help explain the idea in the passage?
questions.answer: One sun can appear in many reflecting surfaces at once, showing how one source can affect many places together.

questions.question: In the mirror example, what does the sun give besides its image?
questions.answer: It also gives light and warmth.

questions.question: What point is made by saying there is no difference between large and small in this example?
questions.answer: Size does not make anything harder for Divine power.

questions.question: How does the passage use the example of one spoken word?
questions.answer: It shows that one sound can reach many listeners without becoming difficult.

questions.question: According to the passage, what allows one word to reach a huge number of ears?
questions.answer: The vastness of creative power under Allah’s permission.

questions.question: Which two examples are given of single luminous beings?
questions.answer: An eye and the angel Jibril.

questions.question: What can such a being do in many places at once according to the passage?
questions.answer: It can be present, look, or enter there as easily as being in one place.

questions.question: What comparison does the passage make between one place and many places?
questions.answer: It says there is no difference for Divine power.

questions.question: What comparison does the passage make between few and many?
questions.answer: It says they are the same in relation to Allah’s power.

questions.question: What can we infer about limits from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is not restricted the way human ability is.

questions.question: What truth about Allah’s power is being explained in this passage?
questions.answer: That Allah can do many things at once with complete ease.

questions.question: Why does the passage begin with examples involving light?
questions.answer: Light helps us imagine how one source can reach many places without being divided or weakened.

questions.question: In the example of the sun and mirrors, what stays the same whether there are few mirrors or many?
questions.answer: The sun can reflect in them all just as easily.

questions.question: What does the mirror example teach about numbers?
questions.answer: A great number does not make Divine action harder.

questions.question: Why is the example of one word entering many ears useful?
questions.answer: It is something people can understand from everyday life, so it makes the idea clearer.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by boundless creativity?
questions.answer: Allah’s creating has no narrow limit and reaches as far as He wills.

questions.question: How is Jibril used in the passage?
questions.answer: He is an example of a luminous spirit-being that can be connected to many places by Allah’s power.

questions.question: What three actions are mentioned for a luminous being in relation to many places?
questions.answer: Being present, looking, and entering.

questions.question: What role does mercy have in the second paragraph?
questions.answer: It is part of the Divine activity through which this wide-reaching action appears.

questions.question: What does the phrase about dominical permission show?
questions.answer: Nothing happens independently; it takes Allah’s permission and command.

questions.question: What is one key lesson students should take from both paragraphs together?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is so vast that one and many are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: How does this passage strengthen belief in Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: It teaches that His power is far above creation and never becomes strained by number or size.

questions.question: What is being described by the title “Second Mystery”?
questions.answer: A special truth showing how Allah’s power reaches many things at once with ease.

questions.question: What natural example is given first in the passage?
questions.answer: The reflection of the sun in a mirror.

questions.question: What other objects besides mirrors are mentioned as receiving reflection?
questions.answer: Bright objects and drops of water.

questions.question: What do all these reflecting things have in common?
questions.answer: They can receive and show what comes from one source.

questions.question: What lesson does the passage draw from the sun’s reflection?
questions.answer: One power can affect countless receivers without difficulty.

questions.question: What human example is used after the sun example?
questions.answer: A single word being heard by one person or by many people.

questions.question: How does that example connect to the main message?
questions.answer: It shows that reaching many does not make the act harder in the way people might imagine.

questions.question: Which angel is named in the passage?
questions.answer: Jibril.

questions.question: What repeated statement closes both examples in the passage?
questions.answer: That there is no real difference between the small and large number of things involved.

questions.question: In one sentence, explain the whole passage.
questions.answer: The passage teaches through examples of light, sound, and luminous beings that Allah’s power handles one and many with the same ease.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s power and quantity?
questions.answer: Quantity does not make anything harder for Allah.

questions.question: Which three words at the start point to why the examples work?
questions.answer: They point to brightness, clearness, and willing submission.

questions.question: In the first paragraph, what is the one source that reaches many receivers?
questions.answer: The sun.

questions.question: What are the many receivers in that example?
questions.answer: Mirrors, shining surfaces, and water drops.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both big and small receivers?
questions.answer: To show that size does not matter to the action being described.

questions.question: In the second paragraph, what spreads from one source to many receivers?
questions.answer: A spoken word spreads to many ears.

questions.question: What does this teach about Allah’s creative action?
questions.answer: It can reach countless things without becoming difficult or delayed.

questions.question: What two created examples of luminous beings are named?
questions.answer: An eye and Jibril.

questions.question: According to the passage, how easily can such a being relate to thousands of places?
questions.answer: As easily as to one place.

questions.question: What idea about Allah can be inferred from all three examples together?
questions.answer: His power is not limited like created powers.

questions.question: Why is this passage important for a Muslim reader’s faith?
questions.answer: It helps the reader trust that Allah’s power is perfect, unlimited, and fully in control.

questions.question: What is the central claim of the Second Mystery?
questions.answer: Allah can cause one action or effect to reach countless places and beings with ease.

questions.question: What image from nature is used to begin explaining that claim?
questions.answer: The sun appearing in many reflections.

questions.question: Besides the reflected image, what else is shared from the sun in the example?
questions.answer: Its brightness and heat.

questions.question: What conclusion is stated after the sun example about big and small?
questions.answer: They are equal in relation to this kind of action.

questions.question: What everyday experience is used next to make the point easier to understand?
questions.answer: One statement being heard by many listeners.

questions.question: What does that suggest about the reach of Divine creativity?
questions.answer: Its reach is vast and not blocked by large numbers.

questions.question: Who is mentioned as an example of a spirit-being with a wide range of presence?
questions.answer: Jibril.

questions.question: What can that kind of being do in many locations by Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Be there, look there, or enter there.

questions.question: What phrase near the end sums up the relation between low numbers and high numbers?
questions.answer: That few and many are the same.

questions.question: What can a student infer about Allah’s command from this passage?
questions.answer: His command is fully effective wherever He wills.

questions.question: What is a good short summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: By examples from light, speech, and luminous beings, the passage teaches that Allah’s power handles the many just like the one.

questions.question: What does the passage try to help the reader understand about Divine power?
questions.answer: That it works without difficulty on one thing or countless things.

questions.question: Why are mirrors mentioned in the first paragraph?
questions.answer: They show how many places can receive from one source at the same time.

questions.question: What other small objects are mentioned along with mirrors?
questions.answer: Water droplets.

questions.question: What is the important lesson from the sun example?
questions.answer: One source can give the same effect to many receivers at once.

questions.question: How does the passage move from a nature example to a human example?
questions.answer: It goes from sunlight in many places to one word heard by many people.

questions.question: What remains easy in the word example?
questions.answer: The same word reaching one ear or many ears.

questions.question: What does this tell us about “many” in relation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: “Many” does not create a burden for Allah.

questions.question: Which examples in the second paragraph are not ordinary physical objects?
questions.answer: An eye described as light-like and the angel Jibril.

questions.question: What can these examples do through Divine power?
questions.answer: They can be connected with thousands of places as easily as with one.

questions.question: What repeated idea appears in both paragraphs?
questions.answer: That one and many are equal in ease.

questions.question: How should a Muslim student respond in faith to this teaching?
questions.answer: By trusting more deeply in Allah’s unlimited power and wisdom.
